If the pair of linear equations in two variables are inconsistent, then how many solutions do they have?
sol: Inconsistent equations represent parallel lines, which never meet, so there is no solution.

questions.q: In an Arithmetic progression if ‘a’ is the first term and ‘d’ is the common difference, then write its nth term.
sol: Each step adds d, and there are n − 1 steps from the 1st term to the nth term: aₙ = a + (n − 1)d.

questions.q: Write the standard form of quadratic equation.
sol: The standard form is ax² + bx + c = 0, with a, b, c real numbers and a ≠ 0.

questions.q: Write the distance of the point (4, 3) from x-axis.
sol: The distance of a point from the x-axis is the absolute value of its y-coordinate: 3 units.

questions.q: Find the median of the scores 6, 4, 2, 10 and 7.
sol: There are 5 scores, so the median is the 3rd: 6.

questions.q:

x − y = 1
sol: Substitute in 2x + y = 8: 6 + y = 8, so y = 2.

questions.q: In the given figure find the values of (i) sin θ (ii) tan α.
questions.fig: Right triangle ABC, right-angled at B. AB = 12, BC = 5, AC = 13. α is the angle at A and θ is the angle at C.
sol: For θ (at C): opposite = AB = 12, hypotenuse = 13, so sin θ = 12/13.
For α (at A): opposite = BC = 5, adjacent = AB = 12, so tan α = 5/12.

questions.q: The sum of first 9 terms of an Arithmetic progression is 144 and its 9th term is 28. Then find the first term and common difference of the Arithmetic progression.
The diagonal of a rectangular field is 60 m more than its shorter side. If the longer side is 30 m more than the shorter side, then find the sides of the field.
sol: Let the shorter side be x m. Longer side = x + 30, diagonal = x + 60.

or.q: In a right angled triangle, the length of the hypotenuse is 13 cm. Among the remaining two sides, the length of one side is 7 cm more than the other side. Find the sides of the triangle.
sol: Let one side be x cm. The other is x + 7.

questions.q: Prove that (sin A + cosec A)² + (cos A + sec A)² = 7 + tan²A + cot²A.
sol: LHS = sin²A + cosec²A + 2 sin A cosec A + cos²A + sec²A + 2 cos A sec A.
sin A cosec A = 1 and cos A sec A = 1, so LHS = (sin²A + cos²A) + cosec²A + sec²A + 4.

or.q: Prove that sec θ (1 − sin θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = 1.
sol: sec θ + tan θ = (1 + sin θ)/cos θ.
LHS = (1/cos θ)(1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ)/cos θ = (1 − sin²θ)/cos²θ = cos²θ/cos²θ = 1 = RHS.

questions.q: Prove that “the lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal”.
sol: Given: circle with centre O, external point P, tangents PQ and PR. To prove: PQ = PR.
Join OP, OQ and OR. ∠OQP = ∠ORP = 90° (radius ⟂ tangent).
In right triangles OQP and ORP: OQ = OR (radii), OP common.

questions.q: Construct two tangents to a circle of radius 3 cm from a point 8 cm away from its centre.
questions.syllabusNote: Constructions are no longer in the current Class 10 syllabus.
sol: Draw a circle with centre O, radius 3 cm. Mark P with OP = 8 cm.
Bisect OP; let M be the mid-point.
With M as centre and MO as radius, draw a circle cutting the first circle at Q and R.
Join PQ and PR. These are the required tangents (each about 7.4 cm long, since √(64 − 9) = √55).

The angle of elevation of the top of a building from the foot of a tower is 30° and the angle of elevation of the top of the tower from the foot of the building is 60°. Both the tower and building are on the same level ground. If the height of the tower is 50 m, then find the height of the building.
sol: Let the distance between them be d. From the foot of the building: tan 60° = 50/d, so d = 50/√3 m.
From the foot of the tower: tan 30° = h/d, so h = d/√3 = 50/3 m.

or.q: As observed from the top of a 75 m high light house from the sea-level, the angles of depression of two ships are 30° and 45°. If one ship is exactly behind the other on the same side of the light house, then find the distance between the two ships.
sol: Nearer ship (45°): tan 45° = 75/x, so x = 75 m.
Farther ship (30°): tan 30° = 75/y, so y = 75√3 m.

questions.q: Construct a triangle with sides 4.5 cm, 6 cm and 8 cm. Then construct another triangle whose sides are 3/4 of the corresponding sides of the first triangle.
questions.syllabusNote: Constructions are no longer in the current Class 10 syllabus.
sol: Draw BC = 8 cm. Arcs of 4.5 cm from B and 6 cm from C meet at A. Join AB, AC.
Draw ray BX below BC and mark 4 equal points B₁ to B₄.
Join B₄C. Through B₃ draw a line parallel to B₄C meeting BC at C′.
Through C′ draw a line parallel to CA meeting BA at A′. ΔA′BC′ is the required triangle.

questions.q: Prove that “the ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides”.
questions.syllabusNote: This theorem is no longer in the current Class 10 syllabus.
sol: Given: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR. To prove: ar(ABC)/ar(PQR) = (AB/PQ)² = (BC/QR)² = (CA/RP)².
Construction: draw AM ⟂ BC and PN ⟂ QR.
In ΔABM and ΔPQN: ∠B = ∠Q (similar triangles) and ∠M = ∠N = 90°, so ΔABM ~ ΔPQN and AM/PN = AB/PQ.
Since ΔABC ~ ΔPQR, AB/PQ = BC/QR = CA/RP.
